papers.title_in_file: Local surrogates for quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections II-V (skimmed), simulation sections including QSVM and Breast Cancer demonstrations, Conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A theory-plus-simulation paper that proposes local quantum and local classical surrogates of trained quantum learning models over a subregion of the data space.

assertions.value: The authors state they numerically demonstrate that any arbitrary quantum model can be locally quantum surrogated with a reuploading-type model up to a certain error threshold within a local region of the data space.
quotes: We numerically demonstrate that any arbitrary quantum model can be locally quantum surrogated with a reuploading-type model up to a certain error threshold within a local region of the data space.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical experiments on a few target functions, a QSVM on a two-class Iris subset and a PCA-reduced breast cancer set; not a proof for all models.
assertions.reader_inference: The word 'any' rests on a handful of small simulations, so the claim is broader than the evidence.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in each of their numerical experiments, they observed an inverse relation between the size of the local region and the local quantum surrogate's accuracy metrics.
quotes: In each of these cases, we observed an inverse relation between the size of the local region and the local quantum surrogate's accuracy metrics.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical trend from simulations in this one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Accuracy holds only inside the chosen local window; the paper notes poor accuracy outside it.

assertions.value: The authors state that for higher-dimensional data, even with localization, the exact classical surrogation protocol quickly becomes computationally intractable because it needs an exponentially large number of quantum evaluations.
assertions.anchor: Section VII.D and Section VIII, Conclusion
quotes: It is evident that with a larger number of data features d, the classical surrogation protocol will become computationally intractable due to the exponential scaling on d.
for higher-dimensional data, even with localization, this protocol quickly becomes computationally intractable due to the exponentially large number of quantum evaluations it would require.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of the exact classical surrogation protocol in Section VII.D and the Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: Benchmarking the Operation of Quantum Heuristics and Ising Machines: Scoring Parameter Setting Strategies on Optimization Applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 2-5 (framework, illustrative example, results, conclusions); appendix parameter lists skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A benchmarking methodology and open-source package (Stochastic-Benchmark) for scoring parameter setting strategies of stochastic optimization solvers, illustrated on a coherent Ising machine simulation and parallel tempering.

assertions.value: The authors state they propose a benchmarking framework, supported by an open-source software package, to collect statistically relevant data when running a parameterized stochastic optimization solver.
quotes: We propose a benchmarking framework supported by an open-source software package intended to collect statistically relevant data when running a parameterized stochastic optimization solver
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own contribution in the Introduction.

assertions.value: The authors report that in their illustrative case, if the number of resources is not allowed to increase, PySA with a fixed parameter setting strategy appears to be the best solver for larger problems.
quotes: However, if the number of resources is not allowed to increase, it seems that PySA with a fixed PSSs is the best solver for larger problems (right plot).
assertions.certainty_reason: One illustrative experiment on Wishart instances, stated with hedged wording ('it seems').
assertions.reader_inference: The authors call the example illustrative; it is not a general ranking of the two solvers.

assertions.value: The authors state the analysis is well fitted for stochastic optimization methods, which they say include quantum annealing and gate-based variational parametric algorithms.
quotes: The analysis presented here is well fitted for stochastic optimization methods, among which we classify the quantum methods for optimization, e.g., quantum annealing and gate-based variational parametric algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the Conclusions.

assertions.value: The authors report that the cross-validated performance profiles come from 10 test-train splits of 50 instances chosen from the Wishart planted ensemble at N = 50.
quotes: obtained from 10 test-train splits of 50 instances chosen from the Wishart planted ensemble corresponding to N = 50
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own experimental setup in Section 4.

papers.title_in_file: Data Complexity Measures for Quantum Circuits Architecture Recommendation
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 2 (skimmed), Section 4 experimental protocol, Section 5 results (tables skimmed), Section 6 conclusion
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study that uses classical data complexity measures to recommend a parameterized quantum circuit layer and its repetition count for classification datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the architecture recommended the best circuit out of 6 for the 14 databases used, with 100% accuracy.
quotes: The results showed that the architecture can recommend the best circuit out of 6 for the 14 databases used, i.e. with 100% accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on 14 datasets.
assertions.reader_inference: The recommender is trained on a table of only 14 rows, one per dataset, so the 100% figure rests on very few cases.

assertions.value: The authors state that the appropriate number of layer repetitions was determined with an error margin of up to three additional layers.
quotes: allowing for an error margin of up to three additional layers
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that fourteen datasets were used, ten synthetic and four real.
quotes: Fourteen datasets will be executed, with ten of them being synthetic and four real datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in Section 4.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation of training hyperparameters such as the type of optimizer and its parameter values is left to future work.
quotes: The evaluation of training hyperameters such as the type of optimizer and its parameter values will be considered in future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit in Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: New Quantum Algorithm for Principal Component Analysis
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section III (start), Section IV (discussion and extension), Section V (start), Section VI outlook and conclusion; proofs and appendix not read
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper giving a quantum singular value transformation based algorithm for quantum principal component analysis, with a comparison to the original QPCA and a covariance matrix preparation method.

assertions.value: The authors state that, from their complexity analysis, their framework performs best when the given density matrix exhibits considerable gaps between, for example, the R largest eigenvalues.
quotes: Upon examining the complexity in detail, we came to the conclusion that our framework performs the best when the given density matrix
exhibits considerable gaps between, for example, R largest eigenvalues.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's complexity-based comparison; proofs were not read by this reader.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no numerical experiment; the result is an asymptotic complexity comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that the number of copies of the density state required has an exponential scaling with respect to R, so their method only works well when R is very small.
quotes: has an exponential scaling with respect to R, therefore, our method only works well in the case where R is very small
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states this limit of its own algorithm, following Theorem 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the complexity depends logarithmically on the dataset dimension n and linearly on the number of data points N, the algorithm would be most effective for a small pool of potentially very high dimensional data.
quotes: since the complexity of our quantum principal component analysis algorithm depends logarithmically on the dimension n of the dataset, and linear to the number of data points N , we affirm that it would be most effective in the context of small pool, potentially very high dimensional data.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the scope of its own algorithm in Section VI.

papers.title_in_file: A Quantum Neural Network Regression for Modeling Lithium-ion Battery Capacity Degradation
papers.what_it_is: A short proof-of-concept paper that fits a quantum neural network regression, run on a simulator, to NASA lithium-ion battery capacity data.

assertions.value: The authors report that, as a proof of concept, their numerical results on the NASA battery dataset demonstrate the ability of quantum neural networks to model the nonlinear relationship between degraded capacity and operating cycles.
quotes: As a proof of concept paper, our obtained numerical results with the battery dataset provided by NASA demonstrate the ability of the quantum neural networks in modeling the nonlinear relationship between the degraded capacity and the operating cycles.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulator results from one study on four batteries.
assertions.reader_inference: The text reports no classical neural network baseline, so the result does not show an advantage over classical models.

assertions.value: The authors state they validated the model on four NASA batteries, B05, B06, B18 and B56, with an 80% training split, on a quantum simulator.
quotes: We chose the batteries B05, B06, B18, and B56 to validate the quantum regression model and the quantum circuit.
The train size was chosen at 80% of the original data for the first experiments on B05, B06, B18, and B56.
This paper uses the quantum simulator back-end provided by Qulacs
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup in Sections III.B and IV.B.

assertions.value: The authors report that as the number of qubits and the depth increase to a certain amount, the RMSE and MAPE indicators drop insignificantly, while a circuit with many qubits and large depth is computationally expensive.
quotes: The obtained results show that the qubits and depth quantities increase to a certain amount, and the RMSE and MAPE indicators drop insignificantly.
Meanwhile, a quantum circuit with a large number of qubits and depth is computationally expensive.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on battery B06 in one study.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Proposition 1 discussion (Section 3), Sections 5 and 6 experiments, Conclusion, Discussion; related work skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A paper that argues quantum encodings lose information between classical and quantum features (the Quantum Information Gap) and proposes a Quantum Information Preserving loss, tested in simulated quantum face and landmark clustering.

assertions.value: The paper proves (Proposition 1) that no Pauli observable and quantum encoding strategy keeps the information when classical features are transformed into quantum features.
quotes: This proposition indicates that no Pauli observable and quantum encoding strategies keep the information when we transform the classical features into quantum features.
The proposition 1 has been proven.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proposition 1 and its proof, Section 3; the reader did not check the proof.
assertions.reader_inference: The result concerns the distinctness of encoded states under Pauli observables; the paper extends it to practical loss of cosine-similarity structure.

assertions.value: The authors report on Google Landmark clustering that QClusformer dropped to 13.20% FP and 35.63% FB, rose to 19.02% FP and 40.28% FB with the QIP loss, and that their classical Clusformer reached 17.74% FP and 38.80% FB.
quotes: its performance drops significantly to 13.20% and 35.63% for FP and FB, respectively.
Nonetheless, by using the QIP Loss function, the performance rebounds to 19.02% for FP and 40.28% for FB, surpassing that of Clusformer
when runs on a classical machine, achieves 17.74% and 38.80% in terms of FP and FB respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from noise-free simulation in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The quantum model is simulated without noise and with fewer transformer blocks than the original classical model, so the comparison is not a hardware result.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments were carried out in noise-free simulation, and that real-world scenarios may involve noise that affects performance.
quotes: the experiments were carried out through noise-free simulation systems such as torchquantum and cuQuantum.
However, real-world scenarios may involve noise within the system, leading to uncertain quantum state measurements and affecting overall performance.
due to hardware constraints, we can only emulate QClusformer with fewer layers/transformer blocks than the original model
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states these limits in Sections 6.1 and 8.

papers.title_in_file: Diffusion-Inspired Quantum Noise Mitigation in Parameterized Quantum Circuits
papers.version_note: File is arXiv 2406.00843v3 dated 22 Feb 2025, stored in the 2024 folder.
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 6 experiments and evaluation, Section 7 conclusions, Section 8 discussion; method derivation (Section 5) skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A paper proposing a forward-backward quantum divergence loss, inspired by diffusion models, to reduce the effect of quantum noise on parameterized quantum circuits, tested in simulation on MNIST and Fashion image classification.

assertions.value: The authors report accuracies of 46.44% on MNIST-4 and 85.32% on MNIST-2, and 46.83% on Fashion-4 and 70.50% on Fashion-2, and state this is better than previous methods.
quotes: In particular, in the MNIST dataset, our method achieves the accuracy of 46.44% and 85.32% on the MNIST-4 and MNIST-2 benchmarks, respectively, which shows better than the previous methods.
Meanwhile, the results for the Fashion dataset are 46.83% and 70.50% for the Fashion-4 and Fashion-2 benchmarks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulated noise in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Absolute accuracy on the 4-class tasks is below 50%, so the gain is relative to other noise mitigation methods under simulated noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that when the number of circuit layers increases, the performance of the baseline dropped dramatically while their approach showed a slight decline in accuracy.
quotes: when the number of layers is increased, the performance of the baseline is dramatically dropped
our proposed approach shows a slight decline in accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation from simulation in one study; figure values not in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the work uses quantum simulation for the circuits and the noise, and that non-Markovian noise models, computational complexity and learning hyperparameters have yet to be thoroughly investigated.
quotes: This work uses the quantum simulation for the PQCs and the quantum noise.
other aspects, such as non-Markovian noise models, computational complexity, or learning hyperparameters, have yet to be thoroughly investigated.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states these limits in Sections 6.1 and 8.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Federated Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Section I introduction and contributions, Section VI lessons learned, Section VIII challenges (first parts), Section IX conclusion; Sections II-V and VII (taxonomy, applications, case study) not read
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum federated learning covering concepts, taxonomy, applications, frameworks, a case study and open challenges.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper presents a comprehensive survey on QFL, exploring its key concepts, fundamentals, applications, and emerging challenges.
quotes: This paper presents a comprehensive survey on QFL, exploring its key concepts, fundamentals, applications, and emerging challenges in this rapidly developing field.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that a significant unresolved challenge is the absence of a mature quantum internet able to distribute entanglement reliably over long distances, which they call a prerequisite for many advanced QFL protocols.
quotes: capable of reliably distributing entanglement over long distances, which is a prerequisite for many advanced QFL protocols.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey synthesis statement with no experiment in the paper behind it.

assertions.value: The authors state that an important limitation is the low viability of full-scale quantum error correction in current NISQ systems, and that error-mitigating techniques can call for repeated circuit runs, an overhead they say would not be feasible for geographically scattered or resource-limited quantum devices in a QFL system.

quotes: an important limitation is the low viability of full-scale QEC in current NISQ systems
But such methods can call for repeated circuit runs
an overhead that would not be feasible for geographically scattered or resource-limited quantum devices in a QFL system.
